title: Torsion-free coherent modules on regular curves are locally free
statement: Let $X$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] scheme of topological dimension at most one and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $\mathcal F$ is torsion-free (its torsion subsheaf $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ of [lem-sc-torsion-subsheaf-quotient] is zero) if and only if it is finite locally free. The rank of this locally free module is constant and equals $\dim_{k(X)}\mathcal F_\eta$ at the generic point $\eta$, where $k(X)$ is the function field [def-sc-function-field].

source.place: Tag 0CC4 (divisors-lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1); constant rank on connected schemes is immediate from local constancy

proof.text: Choose the affine regular neighborhoods from the given hypothesis. They cover X and have Noetherian section rings, so Mathlib isLocallyNoetherian_of_affine_cover makes X locally Noetherian. Localization of each regular section ring at the prime corresponding to x identifies with O_{X,x}, giving a regular local ring. By pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth, coherence gives quasi-coherence and finite type. The finite affine section module of lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine localizes to the stalk by lem-sbc-affine-module-germ-localization. Mathlib Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule transfers finite generation along this localization, so every stalk is finite. This last localization argument is the private proved helper finite_stalk.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1, finite generation and regularity of the stalks

proof.text: Install the given stalkwise torsion condition as Module.IsTorsionFree. The local ring has dimension at most one by ringKrullDim_stalk_le_topologicalKrullDim. In the field case the module is free. Otherwise dimension less than one would make the domain a field (Mathlib Ring.KrullDimLE.isField_of_isDomain), so the dimension is exactly one. Apply lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr, then the Mathlib PID finite torsion-free module instance of lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free. These finite free stalks imply finite local freeness by lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1, proof of the forward implication

proof.text: For the converse choose a finite free trivialization around x using exists_mem_over_iso_free. The proved source theorem exists_basis_stalk_of_over_iso_free gives a basis of F_x. Install Module.Free from this basis; over the domain O_{X,x}, smul_eq_zero immediately proves the stated torsion-free condition. This works as well for the empty basis and the zero module.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1, converse; source module WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.GenericRank, exists_basis_stalk_of_over_iso_free

proof.text: Apply the proved source theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_rank. It holds on an arbitrary irreducible scheme: every nonempty trivializing open contains the generic point, so the number of elements in its finite frame equals the function-field dimension of the generic stalk. Unfolding the source definition rank is exactly the displayed Module.finrank conclusion. No smoothness or properness hypothesis is needed.

lean.statement: theorem regular_curve_torsionfree_iff_finiteLocallyFree (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (hregular : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (F : X.Modules) (hcoherent : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) : ((∀ (x : X) (s : F.presheaf.stalk x) (a : X.presheaf.stalk x), a ≠ 0 → a • s = 0 → s = 0) ↔ F.IsFiniteLocallyFree) ∧ (F.IsFiniteLocallyFree → F.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Module.finrank X.functionField (F.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X))))
